turns.prompt_text: https://ke-complex-modifications.pqrs.org/ There are many possible key combos here, and I would like to use some, I have a wave keyboard with a numpad I plan on mapping as I am not familiar with using a numpad and would rather use it for mappings
turns.response_html:
Since you have a Wave keyboard and want to repurpose that unused numpad, the Karabiner-Elements repository has several specific "bundles" that are perfect for turning a number pad into a macro pad or navigation cluster.

Based on the available modifications on the site and your background in engineering and design, here are the most relevant categories and specific "Rules" you should look for on that page:

1. Transform Numpad into a "Mouse Key" Cluster

Since you aren't using the numpad for numbers, a very popular modification is to turn it into a dedicated mouse controller. This allows you to move the cursor and scroll without leaving the keyboard.

  • Search for: Mouse keys in the search bar.
  • Look for: "Mouse keys (simple)" or "Mouse keys (full)" by tekezo.
  • What it does: It typically maps 8/4/5/6 on the numpad to mouse Up/Left/Down/Right, and other keys to click/scroll. This is excellent for keeping your hands on the "home row" area of your Wave keyboard.

2. Developer & "Vim-Style" Navigation

Given your work in software, you can remap the numpad to handle window management or complex IDE shortcuts so you don't have to memorize awkward finger-twisters.

  • Search for: Vi Mode or Vim style.
  • Look for: "Multitouch Vi Mode" or "Vim style escape key mapping".
  • Application Specific: There is a "Visual Studio Code: Productivity Power Pack" (under the Application Specific category) that includes highly useful mappings. You could assign the specific triggers from this pack to single keys on your numpad.

3. App Launchers & Window Management

You can turn the numpad into a "Stream Deck" style launcher.

  • Search for: Launch apps.
  • Look for: "Launch apps, like on windows + number" or specific "Launch Terminal" rules.
  • Idea: Map Numpad 1 to your Terminal, Numpad 2 to your Browser, Numpad 3 to SketchUp, etc.
  • Window Control: Look for "Amethyst Mode" or "Window Switcher" rules. You can map Numpad 7/8/9 to "Snap Window Left/Full/Right" to manage your screen real estate instantly.

4. Media & Creative Controls

For your design and music interests (like MuseScore or SketchUp), the numpad is great for "analog" style controls.

  • Search for: Volume or Media.
  • Look for: "Fine volume control" (allows smaller increment adjustments) or "Sync Music and System Volume".
  • Design Tools: There are specific "Sketch Shortcut" and "Adobe Photoshop" rules listed. Even if you don't use Photoshop specifically, you can view the JSON of these rules to see how they map tools (like "Brush" or "Zoom") and apply that logic to your own preferred creative software.

How to Apply These

  1. Open the Link: Go to ke-complex-modifications.pqrs.org.
  2. Search: Use the keywords above (e.g., "Mouse keys", "Visual Studio Code").
  3. Import: Click the blue "Import" button. This will open the Karabiner-Elements app on your Mac.
  4. Enable: Once imported, you must go to the Complex Modifications tab in the app and click "Add rule" to actually turn them on.

Pro Tip for Numpads: If you want these rules to only apply to your external Wave keyboard's numpad (and not mess up your laptop keyboard if you have one), you can often edit the JSON rule to add a device_if condition, specifying your Wave keyboard's Vendor ID.
